quoted_tweet.text:
This is actually INSANE. 

Fable 5.2 just created this in one shot, and I did it live on stream. 

I gave Claude one prompt. 

It wrote code that builds the entire room in Blender: the desk, the MacBook, the light, even Clawd.

The laptop screen is a web page Claude built to look like the Claude app, played on the laptop inside the 3D scene.

Then it animated everything itself: 13 camera shots, every single key press, Clawd jumping around, and the sun going from golden hour to night to sunrise.

It rented 10 GPUs on RunPod and rendered the whole thing in 4K in 52 minutes. Total cost: $5.75.

It graded it, added the titles, and made the music and sound effects with ElevenLabs.

text: @rileybrown Is carbon bigger than argon?

I made an 90-second film about Agent Analytics and never opened a 3D tool.

A Cursor cloud agent built it overnight, about nine hours across two cuts, on an 8-core machine with no GPU.

What the film walks through:
- Chat, voice and coding agents in one place.
- Built-in signals and topics on every session.
- Your own evals on your own LLM key, run only on sessions that failed a signal or sit in a cohort you pick.
- Every score is an Amplitude event on the same user as your product, so you can split it by experiment arm.
- Coding agent sessions followed to merged, deployed or reverted.

No, argon is bigger than carbon.

Argon (Ar): Has an atomic radius of about 71 pm (and a van der Waals radius of ~188 pm), with electrons extending out to the 3rd energy level (shell \(n = 3\)).

Carbon (C): Has an atomic radius of about 67 pm (and a van der Waals radius of ~170 pm), with electrons only filling up to the 2nd energy level (shell \(n = 2\)).
